about: The behaviour of @agentcc/client 1.0.1 that only an SDK gives (an OpenAI SDK pointed at the gateway does not), which @future-agi/sdk/gateway keeps, each with the tests that hold it. kept-behaviours.test.ts fails when a named test is gone. 'follow_up' names a behaviour the TypeScript client did not have in 1.0.1 either.

stream_error_frames.behaviour: A data: {"error": {...}} frame on a 200 SSE stream (stream_blocked) raises a typed StreamError with type, code and param, including through the nextjs and express helpers.

tests.title: chat.completions.create({ stream: true }) iteration throws StreamError with the code and message
StreamManager.events() throws StreamError
nextjs streamResponse() forwards the gateway's error code and message
cancels the response body once the error frame is read
express: the client agentccMiddleware attaches raises StreamError with type, code and param
nextjs: createAgentCCClient + streamResponse forward type, code and param and end without [DONE]
late_error_after_finish_reason: events() yields content and usage, then throws StreamError before done
an error body on a JSON answer raises a typed StreamError; a body that is not JSON raises StreamError
a gateway guardrail block reaches the page as a typed StreamError, after the text before it

stream_error_frames.follow_up: event: error on /v1/responses: the TypeScript client has no responses resource yet (it comes in a later minor release); fi.gateway (Python) raises StreamError on it.

request_header_helpers.behaviour: Request header helpers: x-agentcc-config, cache-ttl, cache-namespace, cache-force-refresh, session-id, session-name, session-path, trace-id, user-id, metadata, property-*, request-timeout and timeout-ms.

tests.title: createHeaders sends %s
per-request parameters become headers on the wire and leave the body
client options send session id, metadata and the cache config on every request
a session client sends the session id, name and metadata
returns an explicit key, the gateway origin plus /v1, and x-agentcc-* headers
all three layers: one header, in layer order, the latest layer winning each shared key

request_header_helpers.follow_up: x-agentcc-timeout-ms as a request helper: TypeScript 1.0.1 had none (only the x-agentcc-timeout-ms response reader, metadata.timeoutMs); it comes in a later minor release. x-agentcc-request-timeout is kept (per-request request_timeout).

response_metadata_readers.behaviour: Response metadata readers: x-agentcc-request-id, provider, model-used, latency-ms, cost, cache, fallback-used, routing-strategy, and guardrail-triggered, -name, -action, -confidence, -message and -policy.

tests.title: a plain response carries every gateway reader, configIgnored as a list and clientRequestId
a streamed response carries the same metadata
done comes exactly once, last, after [DONE], with the final completion

response_metadata_readers.follow_up: guardrail-policy as a response reader: TypeScript 1.0.1 had none and the gateway does not emit one yet.

stream_usage.behaviour: Usage: the usage stream event and the final completion's usage come from the finish chunk when stream_options is not set; the SDK never adds stream_options. One usage event per stream, even when the gateway sends the usage again on a trailing chunk with empty choices.

tests.title: usage comes from the finish chunk the gateway sends, and no stream_options is ever added
a chunk after the usage chunk no longer erases it
StreamManager, textStream() and events() complete
the recorded gateway stream (usage sent twice) yields one usage event, then done
adding up the usage events counts the tokens once

sdk_headers_not_read.behaviour: The gateway reads neither x-agentcc-sdk-version nor the SDK User-Agent, so renaming them is safe.

tests.title: every request sends User-Agent futureagi-typescript/<v> and x-agentcc-sdk-version <v>
with dangerouslyAllowBrowser: true the client is built and sends no x-agentcc-sdk-version or User-Agent
